name: QSGD
tagline: Unbiased stochastic quantization: round each gradient element to $s$ levels with probability proportional to its fractional level (256 levels, gradient clipping).
formula: $$\ell_i = \frac{s\,|g_i|}{\lVert g\rVert_2},\;\; q_i = \lfloor \ell_i\rfloor + \mathbb{1}[u_i < \ell_i - \lfloor \ell_i\rfloor],\; u_i\sim U(0,1),\quad \hat{g}_i = \mathrm{sign}(g_i)\cdot \frac{\lVert g\rVert_2}{s}\cdot q_i$$
diff_from_baseline: Alistarh et al., 'QSGD: Communication-Efficient SGD via Gradient Quantization and Encoding' (NeurIPS 2017). GRACE-style quantizer; unbiased so error feedback is not needed. Gradient clipping prevents rare large-norm gradients from amplifying quantization noise.

name: SignSGD + EF
tagline: 1-bit sign compression with mean-magnitude scaling and error-feedback residual accumulation; ignores the compression ratio (always 1-bit).
diff_from_baseline: Bernstein et al., 'signSGD: Compressed Optimisation for Non-Convex Problems' (ICML 2018) and 'signSGD with Majority Vote is Communication Efficient and Fault Tolerant' (ICLR 2019); error feedback follows EF-SGD literature. Highly biased; needs EF for convergence.

name: TopK + Error Feedback
tagline: Keep the K largest-magnitude gradient entries per tensor; accumulate the dropped residual into the next iteration's gradient (EF-TopK).
pseudocode:
1. Augment current gradient with residual: $\bar{g}_t = g_t + e_{t-1}$
2. Choose $K = \max(1, \text{numel}\cdot\rho)$ with $\rho = $ compress_ratio
3. Pick indices of top-$K$ entries by magnitude $|\bar{g}_t|$
4. Communicate (values, indices); reconstruct $\hat{g}_t$ by scattering values back
5. Update residual $e_t = \bar{g}_t - \hat{g}_t$ for the next round
6. Apply $\hat{g}_t$ in the optimizer step
diff_from_baseline: Aji & Heafield, 'Sparse Communication for Distributed Gradient Descent' (EMNLP 2017); Stich, Cordonnier & Jaggi, 'Sparsified SGD with Memory' (NeurIPS 2018); Alistarh et al., 'The Convergence of Sparsified Gradient Methods' (NeurIPS 2018). Strong sparsifier baseline; EF restores convergence under heavy sparsification.
